notes: Lead: growth-marketing platform that generates tens of thousands of short marketing snippets per day (email subject lines, CTAs, SEO meta).

Workload pattern: many small prompts (<= 60 tokens), occasional larger batches for weekly campaign generation (~500 tokens).
Latency target: p95 < 800ms for single-shot prompt generation; can tolerate up to 1.5s during peaks. Throughput target: 50-200 rps during campaign bursts.
Cost sensitivity: high. Currently exploring quantized open models and token batching to reduce unit cost. Wants practical guidance, not academic optimization.
Model preference: open models or small Llama-family variants; open to Redwood curated models if pricing is competitive. No interest in very large models for core snippet generation.
Routing/fallback: wants simple fallback to smaller model for non-critical outputs; policy-based routing by cost tier would be ideal.
Security/compliance: SMB — requires SSO for admin console, audit logs for API keys, basic data retention controls; not yet asking for on-prem or air-gapped.
Quote from customer: 'We need to keep million-req months affordable — if tokens cost double, we can't scale.'
POC ask: 7-day sandbox with typical burst traffic profile + sample config for prefix caching and batching rules (examples).
Risk: procurement needs sign-off at $5k/mo — if forecast shows >$5k, will escalate to procurement (slow).
Suggested Redwood play: promote hosted API self-serve credits, provide a short 'batching & caching quickstart' doc, offer a lightweight cost projection template.
